title: kbmon's cleanup panel answers inside its 10-second limit, because backlog.py tidy's plan reads git state with a fixed number of git processes
goal: kbmon.py --once --panel cleanup reports its state in under 10 seconds with this clone's leftover worktrees and branches, and backlog.py tidy without --apply finishes in under 5 seconds on the same clone

run:
import subprocess as s,sys
p=s.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbmon.py","--once","--panel","cleanup"],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=120)
o=p.stdout+p.stderr;print(o.strip()[-160:])
sys.exit(1 if "timeout" in o or p.returncode!=0 else 0)

clauses.clause: kbmon.py --once --panel cleanup reports its state in under 10 seconds with this clone's leftover worktrees and branches
backlog.py tidy without --apply finishes in under 5 seconds on the same clone

notes: From the 2026-10-24 telemetry and query-log analysis: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --once --panel cleanup (run twice, 14:34 and 14:35 on 10-24) answers 'cleanup timeout 10.0s - no answer in time'; kbmon.py --metrics shows kbmon.panel.up{panel=cleanup}=0 and kbmon.panel.seconds=10.0 (sessions 8.6 s and log 9.0 s are the next slowest), so 7 of 9 panels answer. cProfile of backlog.py tidy: 13.3 s, 118 subprocess runs = 11.4 s; bl_clean.safe_to_remove was called 198 times (11.3 s) from plan() (12.9 s) with 120 worktrees (21 removable, 2.7 GiB) and 73 branches, one git process each (status, merged_into, log time). mon_clean.py:46 collect() calls bl_selfcheck.leftovers, which shares that plan; BYTES_BUDGET_S bounds only the size walk, not the git reads. Goal for the worker: plan reads worktree, branch and ancestry state with a fixed number of git processes (one worktree list --porcelain, one for-each-ref, one branch --merged), however many candidates there are. The repro runs this clone's state: it stops failing once the leftovers are tidied (backlog.py tidy --apply) without a fix, so plant 60 recorded worktrees and branches and count git processes (a git wrapper on PATH) for the check that proves the fix.
